integrator_questions: Did line_loss_events drop to zero with the 50 mm span, and where on each track does the first loss occur?
Is max_error still at the 0.06 m off-track floor, or is it now reduced, and at which bend does the largest error appear?
Does the 0.04 m lookahead still oscillate, or does the derivative term now damp it? Please report steering_oscillation.
Is the remaining failure a turning-authority limit (wheel commands saturating at ±4095) or a control-response limit?

intent: I changed the sensor span from 40 mm to 50 mm (x = ±0.025 m) and kept everything else, because the race showed one line-loss event on every track and the Integrator asked for a wider span whenever line loss appears. I kept body width at 0.12 m, since widening it to 0.18 m would barely move the off-track limit (0.06 m to about 0.0575 m, which still rounds to the floor). I expect line loss to drop toward zero and progress to rise on the s-bend and slalom. If line loss is gone and the robot still leaves the track, I will consider moving the array forward to y = 0.05 to 0.06 m for more reaction time, or reducing mass to 0.5 kg for less yaw inertia.
learning: Hypotheses to test: (1) the iteration-0 failures were line loss caused by the 40 mm span, so widening to 50 mm removes the loss and lets the robot progress further; (2) if line loss persists at 50 mm, the sensor array is not the bottleneck and the limit is turning response, so a forward array or lower mass is next; (3) completion_time on any finished run tells the Integrator whether base_speed can rise. Measurements requested: completion, progress, completion_time, rms_error, max_error, line_loss_events, steering_oscillation and control_effort. Separating line_loss_events from max_error shows whether the problem is sensor coverage or control.
rationale: The race ran off-track on all 60 trials (0 finishes). Progress was only 0.04 to 0.115, max_error sat at about 0.06 (the off-track floor), and every track logged exactly one line-loss event. That single loss, which also occurred on the slalom, is the signal the Integrator's requested-change rule keys on. Line loss means the tape left all five sensor footprints, so the 40 mm span is too narrow for the drift the robot reaches. Following the Integrator's advice, I widen the span to x = ±0.025 m (sensors at -0.025, -0.0125, 0, 0.0125, 0.025) and keep five sensors, the 12 mm footprint and y = 0.04 m. This isolates the coverage question, so the next race shows whether line loss goes to zero. I am not moving the array forward yet, because changing span and lookahead together would confound the result. I am also not changing mass or track, since they affect turning authority and that is not yet shown to limit. Expected result: line_loss_events should fall to 0 or near 0, and the robot should progress further before going off track. If it still leaves the track with no line loss, the limit is turning response, and the next move is a forward array (y about 0.05 to 0.06) or lower mass.
